title: Positive super T-path expansion of polygonal super lambda-lengths in the default orientation and prescribed odd-generator order
author: Gregg Musiker; Nicholas Ovenhouse; Sylvester W. Zhang
source_title: An Expansion Formula for Decorated Super-Teichmüller Spaces
difficulty_reason: The proof extends ordinary cluster T-path expansions to anticommuting triangle variables and requires simultaneous induction on even lengths and odd invariants. It controls sign ordering through fan and zigzag flips, then proves that substitution into a coarser triangulation gives exactly the permitted super paths. This is a full combinatorial construction with cancellation and odd-variable ordering obligations rather than a formal consequence of the classical Laurent phenomenon.
source_version: Official SIGMA 17 (2021) article 080, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2021.080; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Read all of Section 6: single-fan simultaneous induction, zigzag parity/sign checks, and generic-triangulation substitution with the converse path decomposition; also read Lemma 5.15 and the exact graph/path/weight/order definitions. The ordinary Schiffler T-path description and Penner-Zeitlin super Ptolemy identities are explicitly prior background, not omitted new claims. Physical page22 Figures15/16 were rendered and visually checked against the fan-to-zigzag and auxiliary-graph substitution. Only Theorem5.9 is selected, not sign-change, Laurent, frieze or odd-invariant neighbor claims.

statement_scope: Theorem5.9 for a polygon and the corridor subtriangulation crossed by the chosen oriented diagonal (a,b), with the default edge orientation of Definition5.4 and positive ordering of odd triangle generators from Definition5.6. Super paths, permitted teleportation steps and their weights are exactly Definitions5.2 and5.8. The conclusion is the displayed finite path-sum for the even lambda-length; it does not assert a complete super cluster algebra or an arbitrary-surface formula.
